title: Rolling feature-flag cohorts and regional capacity gates for release trains
creator: Jordan Kim
description: Goal: introduce a repeatable, risk-weighted release train pattern that combines rolling feature-flag cohorts with region-specific capacity gates so we can stagger runtime/console/API rollouts without manual cutovers. Motivation: recent multi-region launches hit capacity hotspots and spike latencies for a small subset of customers; current calendar-based windows do not account for live capacity usage or feature dependencies. This initiative will reduce blast radius, provide deterministic traffic ramps, and automate gating decisions tied to capacity signals and health checks. Approach: 1) Define cohort membership logic for feature flags (by account tier, geolocation, and percentage), 2) Implement capacity gate service that consumes per-region capacity telemetry and exposes a simple API for the release conductor to pause/advance cohorts, 3) Integrate gates with rollout automation so cohorts progress automatically when regional SLOs and capacity thresholds are satisfied, and 4) Surface cohort state in Console and Slack notifications for ops and product owners.
acceptance_criteria: Cohort definitions (percent + geo + tier) are configurable in the feature-flag service and covered by e2e tests
Capacity gate service exposes an API and UI that accurately reflects region-level GPU slots and request queues (consumption updated < 60s)
Release conductor can pause or advance cohorts automatically based on gate API responses and manual overrides via Console
A rollout of a non-user-facing runtime config change successfully completes a staged cohort release in staging and in two production regions with no SLO violations
Runbook exists with clear rollback criteria and automated fallback to safe model variant when capacity gate fails

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Gate decisions could be noisy due to short-term metric spikes — Mitigation: smoothing window + hysteresis and minimum cohort dwell time
Risk: Feature-flag targeting mismatch across services — Mitigation: canonical cohort evaluation library and integration tests; fall back to percentage-only targeting if mismatch detected
Risk: Capacity telemetry lag leads to incorrect advances — Mitigation: conservative thresholds, operator alerts, and manual override path in Console
Risk: Cross-service dependency (runtime changes require Console schema update) — Mitigation: cross-team pre-cutover checklist and contract test between runtime and Console
